subject: general
question: Which of the following is located in the west of the Deccan Plateau?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Western Ghats**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Western Ghats, also known as the Sahyadri Hills, are a mountain range located along the western coast of India, running parallel to the Arabian Sea.
 
• This range extends from the state of Gujarat in the north to Kerala in the south, passing through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu.
 
• It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and is known for its biodiversity, being one of the eight “hottest hotspots” of biological diversity in the world.
 
• Geographically, the Western Ghats are located to the west of the Deccan Plateau, forming a natural boundary.
 
• These hills play a critical role in influencing the monsoon weather patterns in India and are a vital source of water for peninsular rivers like the Godavari, Krishna, and Kaveri.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahadeo Hills**

 
 
• The Mahadeo Hills are located in the Satpura range in Madhya Pradesh, central India.
 
• These hills are not situated on the west of the Deccan Plateau but are part of the central Indian landscape.
 
• The hills are known for their dense forests and wildlife and serve as a source of the Narmada and Tapti rivers.
 
 
 
• **Maikal Range**
 
 
• The Maikal Range is located in central India, primarily in Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh.
 
• It forms the eastern extension of the Satpura ranges and is not located in the western part of the Deccan Plateau.
 
• This range is known for the Amarkantak Plateau, the origin point of the Narmada and Son rivers.
 
 
 
• **Eastern Ghats**
 
 
• The Eastern Ghats are a discontinuous range of mountains located along India’s eastern coast, spanning Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, and parts of Karnataka.
 
• They are situated to the east of the Deccan Plateau, running parallel to the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Famous peaks in the Eastern Ghats include Araku Valley and the Nallamala Hills.
